engine.meaning: The dialogue is mostly the original's, but words are spliced into speaker labels and stage directions ("Anyway, HALE:", "Bugger me, MRS HALE:", "Crikey, he gets up on a chair"), and Mrs Hale is made to swear ("my bloody kitchen"), which changes her character. "bugger all of a housekeeper, would you say, ladies, mate?" garbles the attorney's line.
engine.sense: "Sweet bugger-all here" fits nothing; but "Here's a beaut mess" is ironic only by accident, "ay" and "mate" are tacked on to the attorney's gallantry, and "didn't get on properly well" is not a phrase. Several terms strain or misfit.
engine.authenticity: Stage-Australian: tics bolted on everywhere, "Anyway, MRS HALE:", "Crikey, he gets up on a chair", "I see, ay", "would you say, ladies, mate?"; US forms like "I guess before we're through" left in.
engine.register: Heavy in places ("grotty bloody awful quick", "stickybeaking") and untouched in others ("I guess before we're through she may have something more serious than preserves"); bloody and bugger are within vulgarity 1, but put in the wrong mouths.
engine.tone: The quiet, tense drama turns farcical with "Crikey, he gets up on a chair" and "Bugger me, MRS HALE: Yeah, but nah"; Mrs Hale's stiff dignity is lost in "my bloody kitchen".
engine.flow: Broken grammar and jarring joins: "bugger all of a housekeeper, would you say, ladies, mate?", "Those towels get grotty bloody awful quick", openers fused to speaker labels.
engine.variety: "Anyway" is leaned on ("Anyway, HALE:", "Anyway, MRS HALE:", "Anyway, I've not been", "Anyway, seems mean"), with "mitts" and bugger repeated.
engine.essence: The scene is still there under the noise, but the men-versus-women undercurrent is blurred when the women swear and the stage directions crack jokes.

yarn.meaning: Every line rendered with its sense: "Locked up for murder and fretting over her preserves", "the women don't thaw", "Duty's all well and good", "have a go at her for not having things spick and span". Nothing invented.
yarn.sense: Terms fit: "Well, wouldn't it!" for can you beat the women, "Not much chop as a housekeeper", "sticking up for your own", "stickybeaking around and picking holes in everything". "Yeah, but nah, I don't mean anything" works as a guarded no.
yarn.authenticity: Sounds like real Australian speech: "after another squiz round the kitchen", "Grotty towels!", "such a flamin' hurry". "with all the charm of a young pollie" is natural.
yarn.register: A solid level-4 retelling across all speakers, with mild oaths only from the men ("Sweet bugger-all", "flamin' hurry"), inside vulgarity 1.
yarn.tone: Keeps the tension and the women's restraint: "MRS HALE: (_stiffly_) There's heaps of work to be done on a farm." The men's condescension survives in "where would we be without the ladies?"
yarn.flow: Reads as natural dialogue: "I'd say before we're done she might have something a fair bit heavier than preserves to worry about."
yarn.variety: Varied: "squiz", "beaut", "wouldn't it", "pollie", "grotty", "not much chop", "righto", "stickybeaking"; "mitts" used twice.
yarn.essence: Unmistakably Trifles: the preserves, the roller towel, the duty-versus-loyalty exchange ("Of course it's no more than their duty." / "Duty's all well and good") kept.

unharnessed.meaning: Faithful overall, but preserves become "jam" ("carryin' on about her jam"), duty becomes "job" ("Course, it's only their job." / "Job's fair enough"), and the deputy now "might've put a bit of this muck on it himself", a clarifying elaboration; "men's boots" added.
unharnessed.sense: Most fit ("Not much chop as a housekeeper", "the women don't give an inch", "bagging everything"), but "jam" narrows the fruit preserves whose jars froze.
unharnessed.authenticity: Very natural: "wouldn't it rot your socks, women!", "There's a fair whack of work", "sticking their noses in and bagging everything", "the lie of the land".
unharnessed.register: A full level-4 retelling, oaths within vulgarity 1 ("Well, here's a bloody mess.").
unharnessed.tone: Tension kept; Mrs Hale stays restrained. "sticking up for the sisterhood" reads a shade modern and arch for the attorney.
unharnessed.flow: Reads aloud smoothly: "He hops up on a chair and has a look on a shelf. Pulls his hand back, all sticky".
unharnessed.variety: Varied overall, though "bagging" appears twice in Mrs Hale's last two speeches ("bagging everything", "bagging her").
unharnessed.essence: Recognisably Trifles, but swapping duty for job weakens the play's duty-versus-loyalty line.

engine.quote: Anyway, HALE: Well, women are used to worrying over trifles.
engine.original: HALE: Well, women are used to worrying over trifles.
engine.why: A filler opener is inserted before the speaker label, breaking the play's format; recurs with other labels.

engine.quote: Bugger me, MRS HALE: Yeah, but nah, I don't mean anything.
engine.original: MRS HALE: No, I don't mean anything.
engine.why: An oath fused onto the speaker label, and it makes a guarded moment comic.

engine.quote: Crikey, he gets up on a chair and looks on a shelf.
engine.original: He gets up on a chair and looks on a shelf.
engine.why: Slang in a stage direction; stage-Australian and tonally wrong.

engine.quote: bugger all of a housekeeper, would you say, ladies, mate?
engine.original: Not much of a housekeeper, would you say, ladies?
engine.why: Ungrammatical, and a gallant attorney addressing ladies as mate is wrong.

engine.quote: I'd hate to have blokes coming into my bloody kitchen
engine.original: I'd hate to have men coming into my kitchen
engine.why: Makes the stiff, restrained Mrs Hale swear, changing her character.

engine.quote: Those towels get grotty bloody awful quick.
engine.original: Those towels get dirty awful quick.

engine.why: US idiom left in while other lines are overloaded.

yarn.quote: Sweet bugger-all here but kitchen stuff.
yarn.why: Slightly stronger than the sheriff's flat dismissal, though in character.

yarn.quote: Yeah, but nah, I don't mean anything.
yarn.why: Yeah-nah is a little jaunty for Mrs Hale's guarded denial.

unharnessed.original: Of course it's no more than their duty.
unharnessed.why: Duty is a thematic word in the play (the law's duty against the women's loyalty); job flattens it.
Jam narrows the preserved fruit whose jars broke.

unharnessed.quote: might've put a bit of this muck on it himself
unharnessed.original: might have got a little of this on
unharnessed.why: Spells out what the original leaves implied.
Modern-sounding for a period attorney's patronising remark.

summaries.engine: A mechanical, tic-laden rendering that breaks the script format and the scene's tension.
summaries.yarn: A faithful, natural level-4 rendering that keeps the scene's tension; the strongest.
summaries.unharnessed: Lively and very natural, with a few small liberties of sense; close behind B.
